description.value: The study examined whether simple multiplication processing differed between the language in which bilingual participants learned multiplication and their other language, using behavioral measures and fMRI-defined language and quantity regions.

design.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults were recruited; six were excluded and the final sample comprised 29 participants. Participants completed two localizer tasks and an experimental single-digit multiplication verification task in a single fMRI session. The verbal localizer and multiplication task were administered in English and Spanish, with language order alternated across participants. The study used preregistered planned analyses followed by preregistered exploratory analyses.

description.value: Test 14: Picture Vocabulary and Test 15: Oral Comprehension were used to determine language proficiency in English.
Equivalent Spanish versions of the language proficiency tests were administered, including the parallel Vocabulario Sobre Dibujos subtest.
Test 8: Incomplete Words was used to assess phonological awareness in each language.
Aged-normalized classifications were obtained from participants' raw assessment scores in each language and compared across parallel subtests.

description.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults were recruited, with 5 from the University of Texas at Austin and 30 from the University of Houston. Six of the initial 35 participants were excluded from the final sample, and the final sample comprised 29 participants.

no history of cognitive or perceptual deficits
not diagnosed with language delays or learning disabilities

exclusion_criteria.value: failure to complete all experimental tasks

task_description.value: Participants heard two spoken number words, followed by a visual Arabic digit, and determined whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers. Two runs were presented in English and two runs in Spanish.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to determine whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers. They used their index finger if the proposed solution was true and their middle finger if the proposed solution was false.

stimuli.value: Two spoken number words followed by a visual Arabic digit; all words were normalized to 450 ms in duration.

task_description.value: Participants saw a black-and-white line drawing of an object followed by a spoken word and determined whether the word matched the presented picture or not. Two runs were completed in English and two runs in Spanish.

instructions.value: Participants determined whether the spoken word matched the presented picture or not. They used their index finger if the picture-word pairs matched and their middle finger if they did not match.

stimuli.value: Black-and-white line drawings of objects followed by spoken words in English or Spanish.

task_description.value: Participants determined which of two sequentially presented dot arrays contained more dots. Two runs were completed.

instructions.value: Participants were tasked with determining which of two sequentially presented dot arrays contained more dots.

stimuli.value: Sequentially presented dot arrays; easy comparisons had a ratio of 1:3, medium comparisons a ratio of 1:2, and hard comparisons a ratio of 2:3. Dot size was controlled across arrays.

modality.value: fMRI blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signal

instrument.value: Siemens Prisma Fit scanner (3T) at Baylor College of Medicine's Core for Advanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Siemens Skyra scanner (3T) at the University of Texas's Biomedical Imaging Center

description.value: Images were collected using a susceptibility-weighted single-shot echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. Parameters across both scanners were TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 68 s, matrix size = 256 x 256, field of view = 256, slice thickness = 2 mm, number of slices = 64, TR = 1,250 ms, and voxel size = 2 x 2 x 2 mm.

instrument.value: Siemens Prisma Fit scanner (3T) and Siemens Skyra scanner (3T)

description.value: Before functional image acquisition, a high-resolution T1-weighted 3D structural image was acquired for each participant with TR = 1,900 ms, TE = 2.43 ms, matrix size = 256 x 256, field of view = 256 mm, slice thickness = 1 mm, and number of slices = 192.

Preprocessing and analysis of the fMRI data was computed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12). Functional images were realigned, co-registered to a skull-stripped anatomical image, normalized to the standard MNI template, smoothed, and subjected to motion outlier identification and repair.

steps.value: all functional images were realigned to their mean functional image across runs
an anatomical brain mask was created by combining the segmentation products, grey matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid
the anatomical brain mask was applied to the original anatomical image to produce a skull-stripped anatomical image
the mean functional image and all functional images were co-registered to the skull-stripped anatomical image
all functional images were normalized to the standard T1 Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothing was applied to all functional images with a 6 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel
Art-Repair was used to identify outlier volumes
outlier volumes were repaired by interpolation between the nearest non-outlier volumes
six motion parameters estimated during realignment were entered in the first-level modeling as regressors, and repaired volumes were deweighted

model_settings.value: Activation was modeled as epochs time-locked to the presentation of the first stimulus in each trial. All proposed solutions and all participants' responses were included. The time series data were high-pass filtered at 1/128 Hz, serial correlations were corrected using an autoregressive AR model, six motion parameters were entered as regressors, and repaired volumes were deweighted.

Participant averages of accuracy and response time were analyzed in a within-subject repeated-measures design including Problem size, Language, and Correctness as within-subject factors, with Subjects as a random effect. Only trials with accurate responses were included in response time analyses.

estimator.value: Satterthwaite's method was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom for F statistics.

software.value: generalized linear model from the lme4 package in R

model_settings.value: LA+ vocabulary fluency was entered as a covariate of no interest and LA- vocabulary fluency as the independent variable. Separate models were conducted for small and large problems. Dependent measures were language differences in multiplication accuracy or response time, and language differences in brain activation within the regions of interest.

Brain data were modeled based on Problem Size, Language, and the additive effect with and without the interaction between the two. The Watanabe information criteria comparison (WAIC) was used to determine which model best fit the data, and posterior summaries provided Bayesian p-values. A 95% highest posterior density that did not contain 0 was considered significant.
Paired-samples t-tests compared scores across English and Spanish versions of the three language proficiency subtests.
